title: OSHA general industry exit routes and emergency planning practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry practice questions on exit routes, emergency action plans and fire prevention plans (29 CFR 1910 Subpart E), each linked to its rule.

questions.question: Under 1910.34, an exit route consists of which three parts?

options.A: A hallway, a stairwell and a parking lot
options.B: The exit access, the exit and the exit discharge
options.C: A door, a sign and a light
options.D: The occupied room, the corridor and the fire door

questions.explanation: "An exit route consists of three parts: The exit access; the exit; and, the exit discharge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.34, Coverage and definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An exit route consists of three parts: The exit access; the exit; and, the exit discharge.

questions.question: Sections 1910.34 through 1910.39 apply to workplaces in general industry, except which workplaces?

options.B: One-story buildings
options.D: Mobile workplaces such as vehicles or vessels

questions.explanation: These sections "apply to workplaces in general industry except mobile workplaces such as vehicles or vessels."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.34, Coverage and definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Sections 1910.34 through 1910.39 apply to workplaces in general industry except mobile workplaces such as vehicles or vessels.

questions.question: An exit connects five stories. What fire resistance-rating must the construction materials separating it from other parts of the workplace have?

options.B: A 30-minute fire resistance-rating
options.D: No fire resistance-rating

questions.explanation: The materials must have "a one-hour fire resistance-rating if the exit connects three or fewer stories and a two-hour fire resistance-rating if the exit connects four or more stories."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Construction materials used to separate an exit from other parts of the workplace must have a one-hour fire resistance-rating if the exit connects three or fewer stories and a two-hour fire resistance-rating if the exit connects four or more stories.

questions.question: Apart from the single-exit-route case in 1910.36(b)(3), how many exit routes must be available in a workplace, and where?

options.A: One exit route in every case
options.B: Two exit routes placed side by side
options.C: At least two, located as far away as practical from each other
options.D: None, if the building has sprinklers

questions.explanation: "At least two exit routes must be available in a workplace," except as allowed in (b)(3), and they "must be located as far away as practical from each other so that if one exit route is blocked by fire or smoke, employees can evacuate using the second exit route."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: At least two exit routes must be available in a workplace to permit prompt evacuation of employees and other building occupants during an emergency, except as allowed in paragraph (b)(3) of this section. The exit routes must be located as far away as practical from each other so that if one exit route is blocked by fire or smoke, employees can evacuate using the second exit route.

questions.question: An opening into an exit must be protected by what?

options.B: A door propped open with a wedge
options.D: A self-closing fire door that remains closed or automatically closes in an emergency

questions.explanation: "An opening into an exit must be protected by a self-closing fire door that remains closed or automatically closes in an emergency upon the sounding of a fire alarm or employee alarm system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An opening into an exit must be protected by a self-closing fire door that remains closed or automatically closes in an emergency upon the sounding of a fire alarm or employee alarm system.

questions.question: Under 1910.36(d), how must employees be able to open an exit route door from the inside?

options.A: At all times, without keys, tools or special knowledge
options.B: With a key kept at the front desk
options.D: With a keypad code given to all employees

questions.explanation: "Employees must be able to open an exit route door from the inside at all times without keys, tools, or special knowledge."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employees must be able to open an exit route door from the inside at all times without keys, tools, or special knowledge.

questions.question: A room is designed to be occupied by more than 50 people. How must the door connecting it to an exit route work?

options.A: It must swing inward, into the room
options.B: It must be a sliding door
options.C: It must be side-hinged and swing out in the direction of exit travel
options.D: It must be a revolving door

questions.explanation: "A side-hinged door must be used to connect any room to an exit route," and it "must swing out in the direction of exit travel if the room is designed to be occupied by more than 50 people."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A side-hinged door must be used to connect any room to an exit route. (2) The door that connects any room to an exit route must swing out in the direction of exit travel if the room is designed to be occupied by more than 50 people

questions.question: Where does 1910.36 permit an exit route door to be locked from the inside?

options.B: Only in mental, penal or correctional facilities, with supervisory personnel continuously on duty and an evacuation plan
options.D: In any building with a security guard at the entrance

questions.explanation: An exit route door may be locked from the inside "only in mental, penal, or correctional facilities and then only if supervisory personnel are continuously on duty and the employer has a plan to remove occupants from the facility during an emergency."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An exit route door may be locked from the inside only in mental, penal, or correctional facilities and then only if supervisory personnel are continuously on duty and the employer has a plan to remove occupants from the facility during an emergency.

questions.topic: Exit route capacity, height and width
questions.question: What minimum ceiling height does 1910.36(g) set for an exit route?

options.B: Six feet eight inches
options.D: Seven feet six inches (2.3 m)

questions.explanation: "The ceiling of an exit route must be at least seven feet six inches (2.3 m) high." Six feet eight inches is the lowest point a ceiling projection may reach above the floor.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The ceiling of an exit route must be at least seven feet six inches (2.3 m) high. Any projection from the ceiling must not reach a point less than six feet eight inches (2.0 m) from the floor.

questions.topic: Exit route capacity, height and width
questions.question: What minimum width does 1910.36(g) set for an exit access?

options.B: 28 inches (71.1 cm) at all points
options.D: 24 inches, except at doors

questions.explanation: "An exit access must be at least 28 inches (71.1 cm) wide at all points."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An exit access must be at least 28 inches (71.1 cm) wide at all points.

questions.topic: Exit route capacity, height and width
questions.question: An outdoor exit route must not have a dead-end longer than how many feet?

options.B: 50 feet
options.D: 100 feet

questions.explanation: "The outdoor exit route must not have a dead-end that is longer than 20 feet (6.2 m)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.36, Design and construction requirements for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The outdoor exit route must not have a dead-end that is longer than 20 feet (6.2 m).

questions.question: Under 1910.37(a), may materials or equipment be placed within an exit route?

options.B: Yes, if the area is marked with floor tape
options.D: Yes, for up to 30 minutes

questions.explanation: "Exit routes must be free and unobstructed. No materials or equipment may be placed, either permanently or temporarily, within the exit route."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Exit routes must be free and unobstructed. No materials or equipment may be placed, either permanently or temporarily, within the exit route.

questions.question: Under 1910.37(e), when is an employer excused from installing and maintaining an operable employee alarm system?

options.A: When the workplace has 10 or fewer employees
options.B: When the building has an automatic sprinkler system
options.C: When every exit is marked with an EXIT sign
options.D: When employees can promptly see or smell a fire or other hazard in time to provide adequate warning to them

questions.explanation: Employers must install and maintain an operable employee alarm system "unless employees can promptly see or smell a fire or other hazard in time to provide adequate warning to them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Employers must install and maintain an operable employee alarm system that has a distinctive signal to warn employees of fire or other emergencies, unless employees can promptly see or smell a fire or other hazard in time to provide adequate warning to them.

questions.question: What minimum letter height does 1910.37(b) set for the word "Exit" on an exit sign?

options.B: Two inches
options.D: Four inches

questions.explanation: Each exit sign must have the word "Exit" "in plainly legible letters not less than six inches (15.2 cm) high," with principal strokes "not less than three-fourths of an inch (1.9 cm) wide."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each exit sign must have the word "Exit" in plainly legible letters not less than six inches (15.2 cm) high, with the principal strokes of the letters in the word "Exit" not less than three-fourths of an inch (1.9 cm) wide.

questions.question: A closet door along an exit access could be mistaken for an exit. What does 1910.37(b) require?

options.B: Marking it "Not an Exit" or similar, or with a sign indicating its actual use
options.C: Painting it the same color as the wall
options.D: Nothing, as long as the real exit is lit

questions.explanation: Each doorway or passage along an exit access that could be mistaken for an exit must be marked "Not an Exit" or similar designation, "or be identified by a sign indicating its actual use (e.g., closet)."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.37, Maintenance, safeguards, and operational features for exit routes (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each doorway or passage along an exit access that could be mistaken for an exit must be marked "Not an Exit" or similar designation, or be identified by a sign indicating its actual use (e.g., closet).

questions.question: Which employers may communicate an emergency action plan orally instead of in writing?

options.A: An employer with 25 or fewer employees
options.B: An employer with 50 or fewer employees
options.C: An employer with 10 or fewer employees
options.D: Any employer in a one-story building

questions.explanation: An emergency action plan "must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available to employees for review. However, an employer with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally to employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.38, Emergency action plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An emergency action plan must be in writing, kept in the workplace, and available to employees for review. However, an employer with 10 or fewer employees may communicate the plan orally to employees.

questions.question: Which is one of the times 1910.38(f) requires the employer to review the emergency action plan with a covered employee?

options.B: Only after an OSHA inspection
options.D: When the employee's responsibilities under the plan change

questions.explanation: The employer must review the plan with each covered employee "When the plan is developed or the employee is assigned initially to a job," "When the employee's responsibilities under the plan change," and "When the plan is changed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.38, Emergency action plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (1) When the plan is developed or the employee is assigned initially to a job; (2) When the employee's responsibilities under the plan change; and (3) When the plan is changed.

questions.question: Which item is one of the minimum elements of an emergency action plan under 1910.38(c)?

options.A: Procedures to account for all employees after evacuation
options.B: Each employee's home address
options.D: The building's purchase price

questions.explanation: The minimum elements include "Procedures to account for all employees after evacuation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.38, Emergency action plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (4) Procedures to account for all employees after evacuation;

questions.question: Which item must a fire prevention plan include under 1910.39(c)?

options.A: A list of employees' home phone numbers
options.B: Procedures to control accumulations of flammable and combustible waste materials
options.D: A schedule of fire department social visits

questions.explanation: A fire prevention plan must include "Procedures to control accumulations of flammable and combustible waste materials."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.39, Fire prevention plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (2) Procedures to control accumulations of flammable and combustible waste materials;

questions.question: When must an employer inform employees of the fire hazards to which they are exposed?

options.A: Only after a fire has occurred
options.B: Only when an employee asks
options.C: Upon initial assignment to a job
options.D: Only when OSHA requests it

questions.explanation: "An employer must inform employees upon initial assignment to a job of the fire hazards to which they are exposed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.39, Fire prevention plans (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: An employer must inform employees upon initial assignment to a job of the fire hazards to which they are exposed.
